source.stem: Which molecule contains only single covalent bonds?

packed_tags.subject: science
packed_tags.topic: States of matter, particles and water

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: The sugar particles go inside the water particles, making each water particle sweet.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Even while all the sugar remains as undissolved grains at the bottom, sugar particles are already throughout the water.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The sugar is gone; only its sweetness remains in the water.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: The sugar melts into liquid sugar, which mixes with the water and makes it sweet.

intelligence.enrichment: When sugar dissolves, tiny sugar particles separate and occupy available spaces between water particles, so sugar is present throughout the solution even though visible grains disappear. separation and spreading of sugar particles into interparticle spaces -> sweet taste without visible sugar grains The learner explains that dissolved sugar separates into tiny particles that occupy spaces between water particles, so sugar is still present throughout the solution. Dissolved sugar has vanished because no sugar grains can be seen.
